title: fix(plugin-auth)!: Setup → Authentication's switches show what the deployment runs when nothing is saved
body:
Fixes #38098

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — narrowed: with nothing stored, `SettingsService.get('auth', …)` and `GET /api/settings/auth` answer `email_password_enabled`, `signup_enabled` and `require_email_verification` with the deployment's declaration (still `source: 'default'`) where they answered the manifest default, so a published response's value changes for an existing reader on any deployment whose own configuration differs from the manifest default for one of those keys; on a cloud-managed runtime whose deployment declares `emailAndPassword.enabled: false`, a save of `email_password_enabled: true` with nothing stored answers `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION` and saves nothing in the batch, where it saved a row that was not applied; a save that sets one of these keys to its manifest default where the declaration differs now asks the key's write predicates. Widened: `SettingsService.registerDeclaredDefault` and the type `SettingsDeclaredDefault` (service-settings); `AuthManager.resolveDisableSignUp` (public method); a save that sets one of these keys to the declaration with nothing stored is no change and asks no predicate; on a deployment that declares `emailAndPassword.enabled: false` with nothing stored, the ten `auth` keys visible only while `email_password_enabled !== false` (`signup_enabled`, `require_email_verification`, `password_min_length`, `password_max_length`, `password_reject_breached`, `password_require_complexity`, `password_min_classes`, `password_history_count`, `password_expiry_days`, `mfa_required`) are hidden, so a save of one of them is no longer judged for `required`, options or bounds (for example `password_min_length: 2` is now stored where it was refused `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION`), as under a stored `email_password_enabled: false`; a save that turns `email_password_enabled` on re-judges them. The live-status banner drops its declared-off, nothing-saved statement (`declaredOffLabel` / `declaredOffText` copy removed) and the cloud-managed statement is always a `warning`.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` teaches the auth settings page, these switches or the settings cascade's bottom rung; `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx` states the declared default in this change.

## 维护者速读

- 管理员在 设置 → 认证 里、没保存过值时，邮箱/密码登录、自助注册、邮箱验证三个开关显示部署实际在跑的状态，不再显示清单默认值；托管环境同样如此。
- 属于托管云环境的统一登录工作，接着上一轮的提示横幅（那轮只加了一条说明，开关本身仍显示「开」）把开关本身改对。
- 出错时管理员会在没保存值的情况下看到开关显示错误的状态，或托管环境里打开邮箱/密码登录的保存被拒；已保存的值不受影响，可直接撤回本改动。
- 改动了设置决策记录（ADR-0007）的一条级联规则，需要你批准合并。

## What changes

**The seam (service-settings).** `SettingsService.registerDeclaredDefault(namespace, key, provider)` lets the package that owns a running config state what a key takes while nothing is stored and no `OS_*` override is in force. One private reader, `defaultOf`, answers the bottom rung of the cascade from the provider, else the manifest `default`, and every site that read the manifest default now reads it: the cascade walk (`get`, `getMany`, `getNamespace`, so `GET /api/settings/:namespace` and the write-predicate change test), the value a cleared key falls back to in `validatePatch`, and the type an `OS_*` value is coerced to. Asked on each use, never recorded (the startup-registry rule). `undefined`/`null` means nothing declared; a throwing provider is said once at `warn` and the manifest default answers (functional degradation, nothing persisted is lost). A provider that answers a promise is refused the same way (the contract is synchronous; the cascade reads it inline). The answer is not judged against the specifier's type or options: it is the running system's own value. A key or namespace with no provider resolves byte-for-byte as before.

**What `source` reads.** Kept as `'default'`. The published enum (`ResolvedSettingValueSchema.source` in `packages/spec`) is `env | global | tenant | user | default` and admits no distinct value, and the seat ruled no spec shape change. The reading for existing consumers: `source: 'default'` meant "nothing stored, the manifest default"; it now means "nothing stored, the deployment's default" — still nothing stored, and a clear still returns to it. The consumers that branch on it keep their behaviour: `bindAuthSettings` applies only non-`default` sources (`isExplicit`), so a declared default is never re-applied (the running config already holds it); the restore-on-clear pass (`authSettingsFromStore`) is unchanged; the console renders `values[key].value`. ADR-0007 §Resolution rung 4 is amended in this PR (status line + amendment note), per Prime Directive 13. The spec's own account of the rung (`settings-manifest.zod.ts` file header and the `SpecifierScope` comment, `sys-setting.object.ts` header) now reads the same, and `content/docs/references/system/settings-manifest.mdx` is regenerated (`check:generated --fix`); comments only, no schema moves.

**The declarations (plugin-auth, `auth-settings-declared-defaults.ts`).** Re-measured on base `0e361201` first (reverse-verification run below, before the fix): all three differ.

| key | manifest default | declared default (what runs with nothing stored) | measured on base |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `email_password_enabled` | `true` | `emailAndPassword.enabled !== false` | declared `false` → resolved `{true, default}` while `getPublicConfig().emailPassword.enabled` is `false` |
| `signup_enabled` | `true` | `!AuthManager.resolveDisableSignUp(declared.disableSignUp)` (forced off under SSO-only / cloud-managed, then `OS_DISABLE_SIGNUP`, then the declaration) | declared `disableSignUp: true` → resolved `{true, default}` while `disableSignUp` runs `true` |
| `require_email_verification` | `false` | `resolveEmailVerificationRequirement(posture in force, declared)` | declared `true` → resolved `{false, default}` while verification runs `true` |

`AuthManager.resolveDisableSignUp` is the formula `getPublicConfig()` already used, extracted so the declaration and the public config cannot disagree. Registered in `bindAuthSettings` next to the sign-in floor; a settings surface without the method is skipped like the surface's other optional methods.

**The banner (#38094), reduced.** With the declaration as the value, the declared-off/nothing-saved case and the managed/nothing-saved case agree with what runs and state nothing. Left: a value stored on that a cloud-managed runtime does not apply (now always `warning`), and any other disagreement (`warning`). The `declaredOffLabel` / `declaredOffText` copy is removed from all 11 locales.

**The managed save of `true` (#38028).** With nothing stored on a managed runtime that declared email and password off, the key now resolves `false`, so a save of `true` is a change, reaches the `email_password_enabled` save door and is refused `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION` (`invalid_value`, `constraint: { cloudManaged: true, declaredEmailPassword: false }`). The settings pass's not-applied hold stays for rows stored before the door existed.

**Read first (by risk):**

1. `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts` — `defaultOf` and its three call sites (`resolveKeyFromRows`, `validatePatch`, `effectiveEnvOverride`).
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-declared-defaults.ts` — the three formulas.
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts` — the managed describe, whose first case changed meaning (save of on with nothing stored: was stored-and-not-applied, now refused).

## Tests

- New `service-settings/src/settings-declared-default.test.ts` (7): declared value read as `source: 'default'` through `get` / `getNamespace` / the cascade chain, asked on each read; CONTROL key and namespace with no provider; stored value wins and a clear returns to the declaration; `OS_*` wins; a write predicate sees the declaration as `current` (manifest default is a change; re-saving the declaration is not); `undefined` and a throwing provider leave the manifest default (said once); unknown namespace / key refused.
- `plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-live-status.test.ts` (real `AuthPlugin`, real `SettingsService`, real `GET /api/settings/:namespace`): declared off, nothing stored → `{ value: false, source: 'default' }` through `SettingsService.get` and the route, no banner; CONTROL declared on → `true`, no banner; stored value wins both ways and a clear returns to the declaration; managed: nothing stored reads off with no banner, a row stored on before boot is not applied and is stated as a `warning` (en, zh-CN); `signup_enabled` declared off / SSO-only / CONTROL; `require_email_verification` declared on / `email_domain` posture / CONTROL.
- Rework round (contract review S1 and N5): `settings-declared-default.test.ts` adds a promise-answering provider (manifest default, said once), a patch clear that takes the declaration for the visibility map (a required key behind it is not judged; CONTROL without provider refuses `SETTINGS_VALIDATION` / `required`), and an `OS_*` value read as the declaration's type where the manifest declares no default. `auth-settings-live-status.test.ts` adds `signup_enabled` under `OS_DISABLE_SIGNUP` and cloud-managed, and the hidden-key accept set: declared off with nothing stored, `password_min_length: 2` is stored, a later save of `email_password_enabled: true` re-judges and refuses it; CONTROL declared on refuses the same save.
- `plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts`, managed describe: new first case pins the managed save of `true` with nothing stored refused (envelope `SETTINGS_VALIDATION` + field `invalid_value` + constraint, and `400` + `SETTINGS_VALIDATION` through the real `PUT` route); the two cases that needed a stored on now seed the row before boot; the Google case now also carries the `email_password_enabled` refusal.

## Acceptance notes

- Other `auth.*` keys whose deployment declaration can differ from the manifest default (`password_min_length`, `password_max_length`, `membership_policy`, `mfa_required`, session and lockout windows, rate limits; the rows of `AUTH_SETTING_RESTORE`) still read the manifest default with nothing stored, and a `signup_enabled` stored on under SSO-only or cloud-managed shows on while sign-up is forced off, with no statement (unchanged here). Both are carried by follow-up card #38184.
- The served manifest still carries each specifier's manifest `default`; the console's default hint reads the cascade chain's `default` entry, which the declaration now answers, so hint and value agree.
- Open nits from the contract review, not taken here: the `OS_*` coercion type follows the declaration (identical for the three boolean keys); `SettingsDeclaredDefault` takes no context (an optional argument can be added later without breaking); the `differs` banner sentence says "the saved setting", inexact only where the seam is missing or a provider throws with nothing stored.
- No changeset for `@objectstack/spec` or `@objectstack/platform-objects`: their change is comments only, both sit in the fixed release group, and no gate asks for one.
- Self-hosted, declared off, nothing stored: a save of `email_password_enabled: false` is now no change and asks no predicate (before, the sign-in floor judged it as turning off). It stores the value that already runs.

## Verification

<details><summary>Reverse verification on base</summary>

Fix committed; `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts` restored from base `0e361201` with `git restore --source` (unstaged), the three test files run, then restored with `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree` (`git status --porcelain` empty):

- `settings-declared-default.test.ts`: 7 failed of 7 (`registerDeclaredDefault is not a function` — the seam does not exist on base).
- `auth-settings-live-status.test.ts` + `sign-in-method-floor.test.ts`: 7 failed, 65 passed. Failures at the declared-value assertions (`expected value false, received true` for email and password and sign-up; `expected true, received false` for verification), after each case's running-config assertion passed; the managed save case and the Google case fail because the save of `true` is not refused. Every CONTROL case passed on base.
</details>

<details><summary>Local runs at final head 35da5d7b (after the rework round and a merge of origin/main)</summary>

- Dependency closure rebuilt (`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/dogfood^...' build`), then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings typecheck && test`: Test Files 79 passed (79), Tests 1545 passed (1545); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck && test` (tsc, the examples project, `check:test-typecheck`): Test Files 296 passed (296), Tests 6310 passed, 10 skipped (6320). Lock verdict `command-exit 0` for the chain.
- Dogfood battery at `35da5d7b` (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` under the verify lock): Test Files 491 passed, 3 skipped (494); Tests 4148 passed, 68 skipped (4216); lock verdict `command-exit 0`.
- Derived gate families (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 127): `--ran` reconciliation 127 derived, 124 run with exit 0, 3 NOT MEASURED (exit 3, prerequisite): `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` (pinned fixture needs an unshallowed clone), `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples` (read built output of packages outside the closure built here). `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: 14 of 14 artifacts current after `--fix` regenerated the settings manifest reference page. Families CI runs are read from this PR's check-runs, not re-run here.
</details>

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/auth-settings-live-status.test.ts` — 11 passed; the first case shows `email_password_enabled` read as `{ value: false, source: 'default' }` with no banner.
